name: AnyCalib
plain: AnyCalib (University of Zaragoza, ICCV 2025): the camera of one photo (focal length, principal point, field of view) from one predicted viewing ray per pixel and a fit; no checkerboard needed, no gravity. Apache-2.0 code and weights; trained on crops of public 360-degree panoramas.
summary: AnyCalib (Tirado-Garín and Civera, ICCV 2025): single-image camera calibration. A DINOv2 ViT-L/14 with a light DPT decoder predicts one ray per pixel (tangent coordinates on the unit sphere, convex upsampling); a linear fit and Gauss-Newton refinement give the intrinsics of the chosen camera model. Gives the pinhole intrinsics (fx, fy, cx, cy) and the vertical field of view; no gravity.

papers.title: AnyCalib: On-Manifold Learning for Model-Agnostic Single-View Camera Calibration

limitations: Kernels keep CUDA graphs: their private pool and static outputs stay reserved, so peak reserved is ~80 MiB above portable (peak allocated is not); `cuda_graphs=false` or `release_graphs()` frees it.

The fixed 480 x 640 FP16 TensorRT plan matched portable vertical field of view within 0.553 degrees across 2,000 resized LaMAR images. AUC@5 was 13.05% with TensorRT and 13.02% portable under that fixed-size protocol.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: the camera intrinsics `[3, 3]` and, where the model estimates them, the gravity direction in the camera frame, roll, pitch and vertical field of view.
